decision: defined Phase 0 completion as direct evidence for every acceptance claim
why: unverified platforms, camera modes, color paths, and assistive access cannot count as complete
result: open

decision: ran the complete current workspace test suite before changing code
why: the verifier needs a known-good baseline that predates its own implementation
result: 70 tests passed

decision: separated UI proof from codec, color, sidecar, license, and platform proof
why: the initial plan defines two bounded proofs and the code already has the same ownership split
result: architecture comparison running

decision: chose one Phase 0 command with private domain checks and pass, fail, or blocked outcomes
why: separate verifier binaries made callers coordinate one workflow and an external requirements manifest would duplicate the plan
evidence: architect candidates A and B plus independent judge
result: selected candidate A with candidate B internal seams

decision: kept mac-local and release verdicts separate
why: a Mac can prove its native behavior but cannot mint Windows, Linux, NVDA, Orca, or physical display evidence
result: release must stay blocked until native evidence exists

decision: declared Rust 1.95 and added native builds for macOS, Windows, and Linux
why: the workspace needs one compiler contract and each OS must execute its own tests rather than accept cross-compiled evidence
result: local Mac is directly testable; Windows and Linux remain unproved until CI runs

decision: renamed the runtime benchmark binary and scripts to Crema-owned functional names
why: project artifacts must not carry the earlier competitor name
result: all code, tests, and docs use neutral names

decision: converted valid embedded JPEG ICC profiles to sRGB and refused unsupported HEIC color paths
why: showing unconverted profiled, high-bit, PQ, HLG, or hidden-ICC pixels would turn decoder success into false color evidence
evidence: crema-image decode tests;worker protocol tests;thumbnail cache tests
result: valid JPEG ICC conversion passes;invalid JPEG ICC and unsupported HEIC color return unsupported-color

decision: gave thumbnails and viewer images stable asset-based IDs, names, focus indication, and keyboard reveal
why: virtual rows must retain assistive identity and keyboard selection must remain visible
evidence: browser accessibility helper test;cargo test -p crema-app --lib browser::tests::
result: 9 browser tests pass;native screen-reader behavior remains unproved

decision: recorded GUI frame, edit-render, save, and export request/completion events
why: receipt and draw metrics alone cannot separate UI work from editor latency
result: opt-in metrics now expose frame cost and edit operation intervals without claiming monitor presentation

decision: added one stdlib Phase 0 verifier with mac-local and release modes
why: every gate needs a machine-readable pass, fail, or blocked result and immutable evidence path
result: 2 verifier domain tests pass;full mac-local run pending the deterministic fixture

decision: added a deterministic create-only profiled JPEG generator
why: GUI verification needs a public non-private image with stable bytes
result: identical outputs, create-only refusal, 960x640 decode, and applied ICC pass

decision: added prepare, doctor, finish, and marker-guarded cleanup for a real app bundle
why: native UI evidence must execute the built Mach-O rather than a substitute process
result: prepare and doctor report a signed Mach-O arm64 executable; finish correctly blocks without real GUI metrics; cleanup preserves evidence

decision: drove the signed release app through browse, viewer, exposure, save, export, dirty close, and reopen
why: native behavior and accessibility identity require evidence from the real application rather than unit tests
result: originals remained unchanged; XMP reopened at +1.05 EV; profiled JPEG export and GUI receipt passed

decision: allowed grid shortcuts while an accessibility thumbnail owns focus
why: the native run reproduced Right Arrow and Enter being swallowed by a viewer-only keyboard-input guard
result: native Right Arrow changed selection and Enter opened the viewer after the root-cause fix

decision: canonicalized the generated ICC creation timestamp
why: the first real determinism test showed that the profile encoder inserted wall-clock time
result: byte-identical output test passes without weakening the embedded-profile path

decision: measured warm-cache UI work while scrolling a 10,000-item index
why: the provisional 60 fps target needs release-build runtime evidence on declared hardware
result: 1057 frames; p95 402 us; max 1237 us; zero frames above 16667 us; presentation timing remains unproved

decision: made 10000-photo performance a source-bound release-assessment input
why: a one-off metric calculation cannot enforce the same gate on future macOS, Windows, and Linux evidence bundles
result: warm-cache, source identity, sample size, and p95 budget are machine checked

decision: marked Phase 0 implementation complete and release acceptance blocked
why: a Mac cannot supply representative RAF or ORF, HEIC variant, Windows, Linux, display-color, screen-reader, memory, or distribution evidence
result: zero known local failures; remaining gates are explicit blockers rather than skipped successes

decision: fixed evidence aggregation, source binding, malformed TSV handling, HEIC defaults, and phase scope
why: independent review found release evidence could be combined too loosely and GUI receipts could claim a stale source identity
result: every supplied bundle must pass every core and fixture check; prepare rejects source drift; undeclared HEIC transfer fails closed; Phase 4 packaging no longer blocks Phase 0

decision: bound assistive and display evidence to native hosts and made scroll coverage plus remaining performance gates explicit
why: second independent review found one-frame receipts and cross-platform capability leakage could still mint a false pass
result: performance requires 100 frames, 20 positions, 500 traversed items, and 10000 scan-complete assets; next-photo, exposure, and memory remain blocked until measured

decision: refused synthetic next-photo, exposure, and memory performance evidence and validated receipt number types
why: the release assessor must not imply a completion path before a real source-bound producer exists
result: current full-shaped evidence remains blocked; malformed numeric fields become a machine-readable failure
